author: NorthEast News Desk
body: OpenAI will not pursue an initial public offering in 2026, CEO Sam Altman said in a recent interview cited by TechCrunch. The company has filed confidentially for an IPO, but Altman said current safety concerns and the amount of work still ahead make this an unsuitable moment to enter public markets.

Altman said the company is not rushing the process and would go public only when the business and the broader social environment around advanced artificial intelligence are ready. His comments narrow expectations around timing without establishing a new target date. Earlier reporting had indicated OpenAI was considering a late-2026 offering but was leaning toward 2027 amid volatile technology shares and financial pressures.

The timing decision matters because a public listing would expose OpenAI to quarterly market expectations while it faces scrutiny over model safety, security incidents and the cost of developing and operating increasingly capable systems. Remaining private gives management more flexibility, though investors and employees will continue to watch for a liquidity event. The confidential filing keeps the option open; Altman’s remarks make clear that the company does not plan to complete the process this year.
dek: The company has filed confidentially, but its CEO said safety concerns and business readiness rule out a listing this year.
headline: Sam Altman says OpenAI will not go public in 2026
